title: The register
eyebrow: The whole catch, every row linked
dek: 1,508 entries for 1,095 distinct names — every one of them with a link to the record it came from.
caveat_head: Read this before you read the list
caveats: This is the catch, not the family.

Most of the people below are **not** this family. The index does not distinguish *De Franceschi* from *Francetich*, *Franchini* or *Franceschini*, so neither does this page. Where the archive has actually joined a person to a household, they appear on Everyone and usually on a page of their own.
An entry is not a person.

Two rows can be one man, indexed twice from two books. 1,800 raw records collapsed to these 1,508 once exact duplicates were removed, and more duplicates certainly survive under different spellings. **Do not read 1,508 as a population.**

FamilySearch reports **3,652 results** and will not hand them over. Past about offset 1,800 the endpoint silently wraps back to page one and serves it again — HTTP 200, no warning, no error. Everything beyond that is unreachable by this route, and the gap is written up on Method.

429 entries carry no surname at all. They surfaced because a *parent* of the name is indexed on the same record. They are kept, grouped under **Surname not indexed**, because dropping them would quietly shrink the catch.

Within a day of publishing, this page's own de-duplication proved too gentle. A household of nine Moscarda children turned out to be **five** — *Antonio 1835* and *Antonio 1836*, *Stefano 1844* and *Stefano 1844*, *Epifanio* and *Giovanni Epifano* both June 1849 — one set indexed in Italian, one in Latin, neither an exact duplicate of the other. **Matching on a name and a year is not enough**, and nothing was added to the archive from that household.

The 76 rows that shared a name with somebody already in this archive have now been gone through one at a time. **50 were the same person** and are joined — their record id sits on that person's row. **6 were a different person of the same name**, born on average decades apart, and are now people in their own right. **20 could not be decided** and say why, in the row itself. The chips above move as that work is done; they are not decoration.
convention:
Every row here carries the **record id FamilySearch returned for it**, resolved into a link — not most rows, all 1,508. That is only affordable because the id was written down **at the moment the row was taken**, not looked up afterwards; going back for ids later is the expensive version of the same work, and usually it never happens.

One honest limit on that claim: the ids are exactly as the service gave them, but **the link pattern around them has not been tested row by row** — spot checks resolve, 1,508 spot checks have not been run. Where a future entry cannot be linked at all, this page will say why in the source column rather than leave it blank.
